subject: FY28 invoicing options: deferred invoice schedule and multi-year commitment analysis
messages:
From: Elizabeth Rowe <elizabeth.rowe@ennovahealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: FY28 invoicing options and commitment structure

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the introductory call earlier — as we start FY28 planning, my finance and procurement teams asked me to get a few concrete pro forma options from you. High level: Ennova is evaluating a multi-year commitment but we'd like flexibility on invoicing cadence (our finance team prefers split/deferred invoices across fiscal quarters rather than one large annual prepay).

Can you provide: 1) a pro forma showing 1-year annual prepay (with the discount you’d offer), 2) a 2-year prepay option (term discount and how it compares to annual), and 3) a deferred-invoice schedule that shows the same committed $ value but split across quarters (and how that affects the effective discount / cashflow). Also include sample ramp schedules (month-by-month expected consumption and suggested billing triggers) so our budget owners can map spend.

I’ve attached our FY28 budget template for reference. Procurement timeline: we need budget approvals by Apr 15 and a signed SOW/invoice schedule by May 7 to hit procurement cutoffs.

Can Ben or someone on finance run the pro forma with the deferred-invoice permutations? Also who should I expect from your legal/treasury team for invoice terms?

Thanks,
Elizabeth
Elizabeth Rowe
Director of IT Procurement
Ennova Health

Attachment: Ennova_FY28_budget_template.xlsx (Excel spreadsheet, 120KB)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elizabeth Rowe <elizabeth.rowe@ennovahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FY28 invoicing options and commitment structure

Hi Elizabeth — great to hear from you and thanks for the clear ask. I’ve sketched three parallel options below and attached a draft pro forma PDF that lays out numbers at the level you asked for. Ben is looped in to model the deferred invoice permutations.

Quick summary (high level):
- Option A — Annual prepay (1 year): standard annual prepay with invoice at signing. Typical term discount: 10% off list.
- Option B — Multi-year prepay (2 years): commit to a 24-month volume. Invoice structure usually upfront for each year; discount improves (we can do ~18% on a 2-year commit, subject to final $).
- Option C — 2-year commit with deferred invoices: same committed $ as Option B but invoice split across quarters/years per your budget windows. Effective cash impact differs; discount needs to be adjusted because we’re deferring collection. We model two deferred schedules in the attached pro forma (60/40 and equal quarterly splits).

Ramp: we recommend a staged ramp (pilot months 1–3 at 30% of steady state, then ramp to 75–100% over the next 3–6 months). I put a sample month-by-month ramp in the pro forma (tab: ramp_scenarios).

Next steps: Ben will run the exact cashflow math and produce a deferred-invoice worksheet with invoice dates you can drop into your budget template. If the 2-year deferred option looks right, we’ll produce a draft SOW + invoice schedule and route to legal for payment terms and early termination / SLA credits. Who is the procurement contact we should send the SOW to?

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_proforma_deferred_invoices_v2.pdf (PDF, 240KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Elizabeth Rowe <elizabeth.rowe@ennovahealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FY28 invoicing options and commitment structure — deferred schedule worksheet

Quick note from finance — I ran three deferred-invoice permutations against the proposed 2-year commit and attached an editable worksheet. Highlights:
- Baseline list: $1,800,000 annual run-rate (example) for steady state usage.
- 2-year commit with no deferral: invoice each year at signing; discount = 18% -> net effective price shown in tab '2yr_upfront'.
- Deferred option 1 (60/40 split for Year 1): Year1 invoiced 60% at signing, 40% over Q2-Q4 on quarterly invoices. Year2 invoice at start of Year2 with full 18% discount on the remaining committed volume. Effective discount to Redwood due to deferral: ~15.2% (cashflow adjusted).
- Deferred option 2 (quarterly equal splits): Year1 invoiced as four equal quarterly invoices; effective discount ~14.5% after adjusting for collection timing and credit exposure.

We can tighten those effective percentages if you can commit to net-30 vs net-45 payment terms; shortening terms recovers some discount. Also we can include a 1.0% onboarding credit for the first quarter consumption as a gesture to smooth transition.

I’ve attached: deferred-invoice-schedule-v1.xlsx with the three permutations and cashflow charts. If you want, we can produce an escrow/escrowed-funds approach (hold 50% in escrow) for an additional setup but that has admin overhead.

Ben Carter
Revenue Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: deferred-invoice-schedule-v1.xlsx (Excel, 85KB)

From: Elizabeth Rowe <elizabeth.rowe@ennovahealth.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@ennovahealth.com

Subject: Re: FY28 invoicing options and commitment structure — deferred schedule worksheet

On Fri, Apr 2, 2027 at 08:05 AM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Quick note from finance — I ran three deferred-invoice permutations against the proposed 2-year commit and attached an editable worksheet.

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A couple clarifying questions from procurement and legal:
1) If we go with deferred option 1 (60/40 Year1 split), can you confirm termination protection and pro rata refunds if usage materially undershoots commitments due to regulatory delays? We need language for our legal team.
2) For SLA credits — are those applied against future invoices or refunded? Procurement prefers credits applied against future invoices.
3) Can Redwood commit to the same discount level if we shift up to 10% of committed capacity across EU/US regions mid-term? Our capacity forecasts are still a bit fluid.

Procurement timeline remains the same — we need the SOW + invoice schedule to circulate no later than Tue May 4 to get signoff by May 7. Can you produce a draft SOW with the deferred invoice schedule and suggested legal language for termination / refunds?

Elizabeth
Procurement (on behalf of Ennova)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elizabeth Rowe <elizabeth.rowe@ennovahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FY28 invoicing options and commitment structure — draft SOW cadence

Thanks Elizabeth — answering inline:

1) Termination / refunds: we can include pro rata refund language for unused prepaid amounts after a 30-day wind-down window, subject to a cap equal to unused committed value less any consumed overage. We’ll include an admin fee of 2% for early termination processing unless otherwise negotiated. Exact wording to be drafted by legal but the commercial principle stands.

2) SLA credits: we apply credits to future invoices by default; refunds are possible but require explicit approval. We’ll include the credit application clause in the SOW.

3) Regional shift: we can support up to a 10% capacity reallocation across regions without changing the headline discount, provided model family and instance types remain within the same cost bucket. Significant architecture or region-cost delta would need re-pricing.

Proposed commercial cadence (example):
- Year 1 (2-year commit): 40% invoice at signing (covers onboarding + Q1 ramp), 30% invoiced on Oct 1, 30% invoiced Jan 1.
- Year 2: invoice at start of Year 2 for year two prepay (with 18% term discount).

I’m attaching an updated pro forma and a draft SOW template we can iterate on. If that cadence works, I’ll route to legal and our Treasury contact to prepare the DocuSign envelope for the SOW + invoice schedule. Can you confirm who should receive the DocuSign (procurement@ennovahealth.com or legal@ennovahealth.com)?

Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_proforma_deferred_invoices_v2.pdf (updated)

Subject: RE: FY28 invoicing options and commitment structure — approval to proceed

Elizabeth — appreciate the detailed timeline. Redwood is prepared to proceed on the modified two-year terms with the deferred invoice cadence Jordan proposed (40/30/30 for Year1, Year2 upfront). As a commercial accommodation we’ll include: a one-time onboarding credit equal to 1% of Year1 committed spend and the pro rata refund language noted below.

Key items for legal / procurement to confirm:
- Deal ID: EN-4837
- Headline: 2-year prepay at effective 18% discount (subject to final $), Year1 split as 40% at signing / 30% Oct 1 / 30% Jan 1.
- Termination: pro rata refund for unused prepaid amounts after 30-day wind-down; 2% admin fee on refunds.
- Credits: SLA credits to be applied against future invoices by default.
- Payment terms: standard net-30; we can consider net-45 if procurement requests it but that will slightly change effective discount.

Jordan — please route the SOW and invoice schedule to procurement@ennovahealth.com and legal@ennovahealth.com. Ben — please prepare the DocuSign envelope and include the proforma and the deferred-invoice worksheet. I’ve cc’d Ben for ops handoff.

-Rishi Malhotra
VP Revenue Operations & Strategy
Redwood Inference
